text: Hi, this is Brian from Binance Trading and today I'm going to be going over our global markets overview for December. You can find this report and all of our latest@research.binance.com in the first of our research views we take a look at what is called the Santa Claus Rally, which in traditional equity markets is when there is a price rally in the last two weeks of the year. In 2019, unfortunately there was no such Santa Claus rally for large cap cryptocurrencies and the markets generally remained flat. In December, Bitcoin closed the year at $7,200, Ethereum closed at $130 and Ripple closed at 19 cents. This was quite a big difference from the estimations of our institutional clients. According to a survey we conducted back in October where they expected BTC by the end of the year to be at $10,000, Ethereum to be at $200 and Ripple to be at $0.30. Meanwhile, Binance Staking continued to distribute more staking rewards. Six Binance branded NFTs were created selling at around 100 to $300 each. Binance futures continued its fast growth and and recently added the BCH USDT pair with leverage up to 50 and Binance also announced a strategic investment in FTX. Moving on to global markets, we can see that Bitcoin faced a 4.7% price drop for this month, Ethereum faced a 15.1% price drop, Ripple faced a 14.4% price drop and out of the top 10 crypto assets by Market Cap Stellar had the worst performance with a 21.7% price drop. The top three monthly gainers on Binance.com were Waves, Tomo and Zen, which all had over 60% price increases. And the top three monthly losers on Binance.com were HBAR Data and Matic, which all faced over 50% price drops. Bitcoin trading dominance remained above 40% this month and Bitcoin market dominance increased slightly from 67% to 68%. There were two new listings on Binance.com this month which were Vitae and FTT. Binance futures continued its fast growth this month and the BTC USDT Perp contract offer often had higher volumes than the total spot volumes across all pairs. On binance.com the Ethereum USDT perp contract increased its maximum leverage from 50 to 75 and the BCH USDT perp contract was added with a maximum leverage of 50. Ravencoin or RVN was added for margin trading this month and now there are a total of 29 assets supported for margin trading. We recently released a report on staking which you can read@research.binance.com Binance Staking offers zero fee staking rewards and now supports a total of 14 crypto assets. Moving on to views from Binance Trading There was quite a lot of debate this month about whether bitcoin would reach 6,500 or the $8,000 mark first as bitcoin hovered at around 7,250. And we actually asked this poll in our Binance Trading telegram channel and the opinion was split almost exactly 50 50. Bitcoin did end up reaching $6,500 first on December 18, but then almost immediately shot back up to 7,100. And it seems that Bitcoin may be range bound for longer than a lot of people may have expected regarding OTC flows, December started off with a few big BTC sells and we originally thought that this could kickstart some increased sell pressure on btc. But prices ended up holding relatively well and as bitcoin moved sideways there were a lot of sell flows for small cap altcoins. Large cap altcoins like Ethereum and XRP on the other hand saw a lot of demand and had a higher than usual amount of buy flows. BNB also saw a high amount of buy flows this month, especially when prices first dipped below $15 and again when prices dipped below $13. Towards the end of the month, two way flows for BTC picked up. Buyers may have been anticipating a Santa rally or an end of the year rally, and sellers may have started turning bearish after seeing BTC fail to pick up steam coming continuously throughout December. This December was a historically unusually calm December and so it'll be interesting to see whether any significant and sustainable price movements occur in January. That's the end of this podcast and we hope to see you again next time.
